claims.text: The initial alloy has the composition Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
The initial alloy exhibits multiple primary non-eutectic phases.
The initial alloy undergoes a complex multistep crystallization sequence during thermal treatment.
The proposed intervention is replacement of approximately 1 at.% Ni with B.
Approximately 1 at.% B substitution will suppress primary non-eutectic crystallization.
B addition will increase local atomic disorder.
B addition will increase free volume because of B's small atomic size.
The B substitution will increase atomic-size mismatch in the alloy.
B atoms will create chemical inhomogeneity.
The B-induced disorder, size mismatch, and chemical inhomogeneity will disrupt crystalline-nucleus formation and raise the nucleation barrier for primary crystalline phases.
Raising the nucleation barrier will delay crystallization during cooling.
B substitution will extend the metastable amorphous regime during reheating.
The B-modified alloy will retain a higher amorphous fraction after solidification than the initial alloy.
The B-modified alloy will have a higher crystallization-onset temperature upon reheating than the initial alloy.
The beneficial effect will be most evident at rapid-to-intermediate cooling rates, including rapid cooling above 10^4 K/s.
The beneficial effect is expected when reheating remains below the initial alloy's crystallization-onset temperature.
Extremely slow cooling may diminish the beneficial effect of B substitution.
Overheating may diminish the beneficial effect of B substitution.
A statistically significant increase of at least 20% in amorphous retention is proposed as one falsification criterion.
Failure to raise the crystallization-onset temperature relative to the identically treated baseline is proposed to falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The stated reheating boundary says to approach but not exceed the original crystallization onset, whereas demonstrating an increased crystallization-onset temperature by DSC requires heating through the original onset and continuing until the modified alloy crystallizes.
